reviews.review: once you get the hang this game is fun
When I wake up thinking about a game, I know its a good one.

The Time walls are a disgusting tactic to force people to just suffer though things and not make any progression as they play. Bogging down progress for hours on end and even days does not make anything enjoyable about this game and it's a shame as it has been around for a while. But devs are going to be scummy and force people to shell out money to tear down the walls.

This is not a solo-player game.  It can be played solo (and, in many cases, *must* be played solo), but if you do not have a community you play with (or find one fast) you may not play this game very long.  Imo, this game is entirely for PvP'rs.  Most of the content is technically PvE, but (speaking as a solo-player myself) without a bit of friendly rivalry and comradery there is not much incentive to level up in the game, even considering the fact that many of the QoL features are only available to high-level players.

I like the graphics, that the game works well on my old dial-up connection (the only internet available at my residence), and I even appreciate much of the consideration the devs give to their product which ultimately makes playing this game a pleasant experience (e.g. no progress-destroying bugs, although they are still experiencing difficulties in cross-platform play, among other wyrd issues).

But, on the other hand, I have found the lore and story somewhat wanting, and even some of that content to be unreasonably difficult by design (viz. throwing you back to lvl 0, for one part of the story-line, and pitting you against 3 final-bosses and their lackeys and expecting you to win).

It's no RPG, rather more of a hack-and-slash game that lives up to it's reputation as a top-10 most-hours-spent-grinding game, --- both being major turn-offs in my book, --- but as long as I still have friends to play this game with, I too will play it as an easy subject of interaction.  And those grounds alone do I recommend this game.
